paragraphs: Rav bar Sheva. Before Rav Kahana: Menahot 37, end of b. Rava (it should read Rav) bar Sheva said to Rav Kahana: Mo'ed Katan 26a. He expounded before Rav Kahana, and they laughed at him. Rav Kahana said, ‘A great man has said something; do not laugh at him’: Berakhot 19b. He happened to come to Rav Nahman's house and did not eat liver boiled in hot water, etc. Rav Nahman said, ‘Make Sheva swallow it’: Hullin 111a:5. See Arukh, entry גם, what it writes there. Rav bar Sheva challenged Rav Pappa: Eruvin 33b. In Shevuot 30b, Rav bar Sherevya (so in two printings; perhaps it is a scribal error and should read bar Sheva, because no other mention of him is found) had a lawsuit before Rav Pappa, who seated him and also seated his opponent. He happened to come to Ravina, and Ravina did not interrupt Hallel to greet him, because he was not important in his eyes: Berakhot 14a. In Shabbat 140a, ‘Rava bar Sheva before Ravina’ is a scribal error, and should read ‘Rav bar Sheva’ in all the aforementioned places. She'erit Yosef brought him among Rav's pupils; he erred. Rav died in the year 4003 from creation, and Rav Yehudah died in 4060. Rava was born on the day Rav Yehudah died; Rav Pappa was Rava's pupil, and Rav bar Sheva challenged Rav Pappa as a pupil does his teacher. How could he have been Rav's pupil? Apart from this, whence did he get this prophetic knowledge? We do not find anywhere in the entire Talmud that Rav bar Sheva spoke in Rav's name.
